result.summary: A narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and mature street trees on both sides. Parallel parking is present along both curbs, which provides a buffer but also creates visual obstructions for pedestrians crossing the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the street significantly limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street along the curb line.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway with Obstacles
hazards.description: The sidewalk is relatively narrow and contains street trees and utility poles, which may impede pedestrians with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalks on both the left and right sides.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with brick row houses and a wide sidewalk composed of concrete and brick sections. A large mature tree provides shade but causes some minor pavement cracking, while parked cars provide a buffer between pedestrians and the narrow roadway.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and lifting of the concrete sidewalk near the base of the large tree creates a potential tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left, near the tree trunk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars and the large tree trunk block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Level or replace the cracked concrete sections near the tree to ensure a smooth, accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and personal security for pedestrians during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: If a crossing is designated, curb extensions would improve visibility by allowing pedestrians to see past parked cars before entering the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While the narrow roadway naturally limits vehicle speeds, the high density of on-street parking creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits visibility between drivers and pedestrians, particularly at potential crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: Personal furniture (chairs) placed on the sidewalk reduces the effective walking width.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers and to shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossings with high-visibility paint to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The street features a continuous sidewalk with street trees and a curb ramp with tactile paving, indicating a baseline level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the presence of a large vehicle parked directly at the corner creates a significant visual obstruction, and the lack of marked crosswalks reduces pedestrian priority.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large white pickup truck is parked directly next to the curb ramp, completely blocking the view of the roadway for pedestrians and making them invisible to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground right, adjacent to the curb ramp

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians at the curb ramp and approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to physically prevent parking at the corner, shorten the crossing distance, and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the travel lane.
